subject: Request: Carveout to batch job finalization guarantee / async SLA
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cloudmart.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: ops@cloudmart.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: carveout for large async inference runs (job finalization guarantee)

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency numbers on interactive calls. We're evaluating Redwood for a large batch migration (nightly SKU scoring of 10–20M items). One outstanding procurement blocker: the standard hosted SLA focuses on per-request latency and uptime, but our architecture relies on asynchronous batch jobs with a guaranteed "job finalization" window (we need an explicit commitment that jobs will complete within N hours, with clear retry semantics and idempotency guarantees).

Specifically, our asks:
- A committed job completion window for async submissions (our baseline ask: 24 hours end-to-end from job submission to final status).
- Clear retry model: backoff strategy Redwood will apply when internal transient failures occur, and whether retries count against our credits/usage.
- Idempotency guarantees: an API-level recommended approach (idempotency key TTL, dedupe semantics) to ensure duplicate processing is avoided across retries and resubmissions.
- Remediation credits or SLA credits if job finalization exceeds the committed window repeatedly (we can provide a proposed metric and thresholds).

We've attached a small sample of job payloads and logs for a representative run, plus a draft addendum we sometimes use with other vendors (SLA_Addendum_CloudMart_Draft.pdf).

Can you let me know whether Redwood can provide a carveout or an addendum for batch finalization time, and if so what the technical constraints would be? If needed we can accept a larger window for peak periods (e.g., 36–48 hours) if it's accompanied by an automatic retry policy and dedupe controls.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Senior Procurement Manager | CloudMart
procurement@cloudmart.com
+1 (415) 555-0193

Attachments: CloudMart_batch_logs_20270301.zip (zip, 2.3 MB), SLA_Addendum_CloudMart_Draft.pdf (pdf, 210 KB)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cloudmart.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for large async inference runs (job finalization guarantee)

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the artifacts, appreciated.

I'm looping Rishi to confirm the runtime/ops constraints and Marissa to flag potential commercial addendum language. High level: Redwood does offer async/batch primitives (job enqueue, status callbacks, integration with object storage) but we currently do not publish a universal SLA specifically for multi-million item batch finalization on hosted shared capacity. That said, we have three levers we can offer:

1) Contracted reserved capacity (Dedicated) with a job completion SLO baked into the reserved pool (most straightforward for strict windows).
2) Addendum for hosted with a staged acceptance: allow an extended completion window (e.g., 36h) with remediation credits if missed X% of jobs per month.
3) Technical guardrails on retries/idempotency we can document and enforce to minimize reprocessing risk.

Rishi — can you sanity-check the proposed technical behavior below and suggest default parameters (idempotency TTL, recommended max retries, backoff) for a 36h window on a job profile like the attached? Also flag any operational caveats (e.g., KV cache size, GC, retention) that would materially affect guarantees.

Elena — we can set up a short technical working session if you'd like. If your team is comfortable with a 36h staged window for the first 60 days we can put that into a hosted addendum while we evaluate Dedicated capacity.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Attachment referenced: SLA_Addendum_CloudMart_Draft.pdf

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cloudmart.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 11:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for large async inference runs (job finalization guarantee)

Folks — quick technical response after reviewing the logs. TL;DR: we can support a 36-hour committed window on hosted with the following recommended constraints and trade-offs.

Quoted for context:
> On Mon, 1 Mar 2027 at 09:12, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cloudmart.com> wrote:
> > Our baseline ask: 24 hours end-to-end from job submission to final status.
> > Clear retry model ... and idempotency guarantees ...
>
Recommendations and caveats:
1) Job model and idempotency
- Use a client-generated idempotency key (Idempotency-Key header) per logical job. Redwood will store idempotency metadata for up to 14 days for hosted; we can extend to 30 days under contract.
- Behavior: if we receive a duplicate job with same idempotency key and identical job signature, we will return stored final status and not re-execute unless the job is explicitly invalidated by the client.

2) Retry semantics
- Retries will follow an exponential backoff (base 30s, factor 2, max interval 1 hour) and up to N attempts where N defaults to 8 for hosted.
- Retries due to infra transient errors are performed by our scheduler and do not consume extra customer credits for tokens that are reprocessed by the runtime (we will not bill duplicated token compute for scheduled internal retries). However, retries initiated by duplicate client submissions will be billed as new work.

3) Completion window and operational limits
- For the attached job profile (10–20M small payloads, average seq len 64), a realistic hosted completion SLO is 36 hours with a soft-capacity window during peak; we can offer remediation credits if >5% of jobs exceed 36 hours in a rolling 30-day window.
- For stricter guarantees (24h or lower) we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) or a hybrid approach where large jobs are routed to dedicated capacity.

4) Idempotency TTL / dedupe storage implications
- Extending idempotency storage increases metadata retention and operational costs. If CloudMart needs 30-day dedupe, that will need to be included in the addendum (we can propose a fixed per-month metadata fee or absorb under a larger committed spend).

5) Failure modes and monitoring
- We'll export job-level traces to your S3/GCS bucket and provide JobStatus webhooks. We'll include a job-level error taxonomy (transient/retryable, permanent/fatal).

Next steps I suggest:
- Provide a 24–72 hour sample job submission (payload + manifest) so we can run a capacity simulation to confirm the 36h estimate.
- If acceptable, drafting an addendum that describes idempotency-key semantics, storage TTL, retry/backoff defaults, and the remediation credit formula (e.g., 5% misses => 10% credit, >10% => 25% credit).

Happy to discuss in a 30-min call — I'm available Wed/Thu afternoon PT.

— Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cloudmart.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for large async inference runs (job finalization guarantee)

Thanks Lauren & Rishi — this is helpful and in line with what procurement expected. A couple quick clarifications before the working session:

- 36 hours with a 5% miss remediation threshold sounds workable as a starting point. We can accept the extended hosted window so long as there is a clear ramp plan to 24 hours (or migration to Dedicated) within 90 days of go-live.
- Please confirm in writing that internal scheduler retries will not be double-billed — that's a key procurement ask.
- We'll prepare a 48-hour sample submission and the manifest Rishi requested; can you confirm the preferred bucket + ACLs for logs and the format for the idempotency-key header?

If those look OK we'll ask legal to review the addendum (SLA_Addendum_CloudMart_Draft.pdf) and aim to circulate a redline next week. DocuSign timeline: if we can get the addendum agreed and countersigned within two weeks, procurement will finalize the initial 6-month commitment.

Elena
Senior Procurement Manager | CloudMart
